title: Regularization by a functorial saturated log blowup tower
statement: Fix the monoidal resolution rule induced by the saturated smooth-functorial fan resolution of [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization]. For every Noetherian separated fs log regular scheme $(X,M)$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], [pqf-def-locnoeth], this rule gives a finite tower of saturated log blowups with regular log regular source [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Its underlying scheme tower is a tower of normalized blowups, with finite normalization maps, and is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. It is an isomorphism on the locus where $X$ is already regular. The construction is compatible with automorphisms and, up to contraction of unit-center stages, with strict pullback between the indicated schemes: the strict-transform tower is the scheme pullback. The comparisons retain ordered center ideals and respect composition. All stages are Noetherian and normal. If $X$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], so are the stages, and the composite is birational, meaning an isomorphism on dense open subschemes. The statement allows disconnected $X$ and does not assume excellence. Here a normalized blowup is an ordinary blowup followed by componentwise normalization in its function fields [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-sc-normalization].

source.place: VIII Theorems 3.3.15 and 3.4.9, §§3.4.5--3.4.8, printed pp.107--112; finiteness of saturations explained again in 5.3.11, p.126.

proof.text: The hypotheses give quasi-compactness and local Noetherianity. By [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart], each geometric characteristic $P$ is sharp fs. Its group completion is torsion free: if $ng=0$ for $n>0$, saturation puts both $g$ and $-g$ in $P$, and sharpness then gives $g=0$. Thus the chart and descent results below apply. Fix precisely the rule $\mathcal R$ of [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization]. Let $c:(V,\overline N)\to F$ be a global fan chart of a quasi-compact member $(V,N)$. First make $F$ admissible for $\mathcal R$, which is defined only on torsion-free fans with a finite affine cover. Each $v\in V$ has a neighbourhood mapping into the affine localization $F_{c(v)}$; by quasi-compactness finitely many of these cover $V$, so $c$ factors through their union $F'$, an open subfan with a finite affine cover, and $c$ is still a fan chart. The stalk of $F$ at $c(v)$ is $\overline N_v$, fs and sharp; the stalk at any other point of $F_{c(v)}$ is, by the affine model in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], the sharpening of the localization of that fs monoid at a face, whose group completion is free by [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening]. Thus $F'$ is torsion free and $\mathcal R(F')$ is defined; by the open-localization compatibility of [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization] another finite subcover changes it only by canonical contracted identifications. Pull back the ordered tower $\mathcal R(F')$ using [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii). At stage $i$ the center is the inverse image in $N_i$ of the ideal generated by $c_i^{-1}J_i$ in $\overline N_i$, where $J_i$ is the fan center. Contract whole-monoid centers. Such a blowup is the identity, since the identity already makes the ideal invertible and satisfies its universal property [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

source.place: VIII 3.3.14--3.3.15, pp.109--110; construction of the charted rule.

proof.text: Compare two fan charts, or the source and target charts of a strict map. [lem-trf-strict-fan-chart-local-comparison] identifies their localized fans around each source point, with equality of the chart maps after that identification. Smooth functoriality of $\mathcal R$ applies to these localizations and isomorphisms [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization]. Pulling back the identified ordered centers gives the same ideals and towers on this neighborhood by [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii). Uniqueness of the saturated log blowup [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] makes the comparisons agree on further restrictions and under composition, level by level. For finite disjoint unions use the disjoint union fan and the component-inclusion comparisons of $\mathcal R$. In particular these comparisons hold for strict etale maps, so [lem-trf-functorial-log-blowup-etale-descent] applies. It gives one finite global tower $\mathcal T(X,M)$, including its actual nonempty coherent ordered centers, whose contracted restriction to each fan-chart neighborhood is the tower just constructed. No independent choices of resolutions on different charts are made.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110, localization, finite disjoint unions and descent.

proof.text: Induct on the finite tower, starting with log regular $X_0=X$. For a center $\mathcal I_i$, [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] gives its finite-type quasi-coherent ring ideal $J_i=\alpha(\mathcal I_i)\mathcal O_{X_i}$, the fine log blowup $X_i^0$, the saturated one $X_{i+1}$ and the finite map $s_i:X_{i+1}\to X_i^0$, all commuting with strict etale restriction. On a strict etale affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with monoid $P$ and generators $E$, the saturated charts are $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e^{\rm sat}])$, where $Q_e=\langle P,h-e\ (h\in E)\rangle\subset P^{\rm gp}$; these monoids have the same group completion as $P$. Therefore [lem-trf-log-regular-toric-refinement] makes these charts log regular and locally Noetherian; this is a stalkwise condition in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], so $X_{i+1}$ is log regular. Cover $X_i$ by such charts. On each, $X_i^0\times_{X_i}\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the fine log blowup of the chart, $J_i\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}=(\alpha(e):e\in E)$, and [lem-trf-monomial-rees-chart-comparison] identifies it with $\operatorname{Bl}_{(\alpha(e))}\operatorname{Spec}A$. Each $\alpha(e)$ is a non-zero-divisor: by [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure] it is a unit on a dense open and the local rings are domains, so a germ killed by it vanishes on a neighbourhood meeting that open and is zero. Hence [lem-trf-etale-blowup-chart-descent], applied to $Z=X_i^0$ with no compatibility needed between the chart isomorphisms, gives a canonical $X_i$-isomorphism $X_i^0\simeq B_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}X_i$. Thus $s_i:X_{i+1}\to B_i$ is finite, without any excellence assumption.

We also induct on Noetherianity. For the ordinary blowup of the finite-type quasi-coherent $J_i$, [lem-sfb-blowup-rees-symmetric-presentation] gives $B_i=\operatorname{Proj}_{X_i}(\bigoplus J_i^n)$ and a surjection $\operatorname{Sym}(J_i)\twoheadrightarrow\bigoplus J_i^n$. The surjective-map clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] gives a closed immersion $B_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_{X_i}(J_i)$, proving projectivity in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], for disconnected inputs too. The finite map $s_i$ is projective by [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle]. Since $X_i$ is Noetherian, it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Thus [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-composition] makes $b_i:X_{i+1}\to X_i$ projective. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper] it is proper, hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X_{i+1}$ Noetherian, completing the induction. Repeated application of the same composition lemma over the Noetherian base $X$ proves projectivity of the full composite. A length-zero tower is the identity, presented as the projective bundle of the rank-one module.

source.place: VIII 3.4.8, pp.111--112; Stacks Tags 02NS, 07ZK, 0C4P and 01T6 for scheme projectivity and Noetherianity.

proof.text: At every stage normality and an open dense triviality locus $U_i$ follow from [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure]. As $X_i$ is Noetherian, [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components] decomposes it into finitely many disjoint open and closed normal integral components. Restrict a stage to each such component. Its log ideal remains nonempty coherent, so [lem-trf-log-blowup-normalization] identifies the restriction with the normalization of its ordinary blowup in the component's function field, and gives $U_{i+1}=b_i^{-1}U_i\simeq U_i$. These restrictions really are the given blowup: open restriction is strict and the universal property in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] uniquely identifies the two universal objects. The same applies to ordinary blowups on open components. On each component $C$, apply [lem-trf-finite-normal-blowup-recognition] to the finite map $s_i:X_{i+1}|_C\to B_i|_C$ of Step 3, with $U$ the triviality locus of $C$: $J_i|_U=\mathcal O_U$, the inverse image of $U$ is dense and maps isomorphically to $U$ by the normalization lemma just cited, and $X_{i+1}$ has normal domain local rings. It gives the normalization identification with $s_i=\nu\circ(X_{i+1}|_C\simeq(B_i|_C)^\nu)$. Consequently the global stage is exactly the componentwise normalized blowup of $J_i$, and its normalization map is the finite map $s_i$. If $X$ is integral, the cited normalization identification keeps every stage integral, inductively. Its dense triviality locus is the inverse image of $U_0$ and maps isomorphically to $U_0$. Thus the composite is birational in the stated dense-open sense.

On any chart, [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii) identifies each terminal characteristic with a stalk of the terminal fan of $\mathcal R$. That fan is smooth by [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization], so these stalks are free $\mathbf N^r$. Descent in Step 2 retains these identifications on the strict etale cover and contraction removes only identity stages. Hence every characteristic of $X_n$ is free. Since Step 3 gives log regularity, [lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary] implies that $X_n$ is regular.

For a regular point $x$ of $X$, [lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary] makes its characteristic $\mathbf N^r$. [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart] supplies an etale neighborhood with that chart, and [lem-trf-monoid-chart-characteristic-fan] gives its fan chart to $S(\mathbf N^r)$. The chosen fan rule is trivial on a point: every nonempty ideal of its zero monoid is whole, and the identity comparison with its own contracted tower forces its length to be zero. The map $S(\mathbf N^r)\to S(0)$ is smooth, because each stalk map is $0\to\mathbf N^a$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Smooth functoriality [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization] therefore makes its tower trivial too. Steps 1--2 now identify the restricted tower near $x$ with the trivial tower. Thus every center becomes whole there and each stage is the identity by its universal property [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. These neighborhoods lie over regular points only, since their free-characteristic log regular local rings are regular by the same criterion; their images are open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] and cover the regular locus. The tower is consequently an isomorphism over that locus, not merely over the log triviality locus.

source.place: VIII 3.4.4, p.110, and 3.3.15; regular-locus invariance argument as in 2.3.14, p.94.

proof.text: Let $f:(Y,N)\to(X,M)$ be any strict map between the schemes in the statement. The local comparison argument of Step 2 applies to $f$, without an etale assumption: [lem-trf-strict-fan-chart-local-comparison] is stated for arbitrary strict maps of Zariski log schemes. Choose strict etale chart neighborhoods of target and source using [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](i); their comparisons reduce to that statement. It gives equality of the contracted ordered pullback towers locally. The canonical level comparisons glue: at each retained stage the pulled-back center is fixed and the universal property [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] makes its comparison unique. Unit-center stages are identity universal objects and are deleted; later centers are transported through those identities. Thus the local comparisons have the cocycle and descend, just as in Step 2. They identify $\mathcal T(Y,N)$ with the contraction of $f^*\mathcal T(X,M)$. Their centers and their order are the specified pulled-back ones. Applying the same uniqueness to two consecutive strict maps shows that their comparison composite equals the comparison for the composite. This includes log automorphisms.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110, restricted to strict maps; 3.4.9.

proof.text:
Finally check that each uncontracted strict-pullback square is a scheme pullback, rather than only an fs pullback. On affine charts a strict map uses the same monoid $P$, center generators $E$, and saturated chart monoid $Q_e^{\rm sat}$. [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] gives the two chart rings $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e^{\rm sat}]$ and $A'\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e^{\rm sat}]$. The coefficient map identifies the second with
$$A'\otimes_A\bigl(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e^{\rm sat}]\bigr),\qquad a'\otimes(a\otimes z^q)\longmapsto a'f(a)\otimes z^q,$$
with inverse $a'\otimes z^q\mapsto a'\otimes(1\otimes z^q)$. Globally, the saturated blowup $Y_s\to X_s$ given by the universal property [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] induces a canonical map $\kappa:Y_s\to X_s\times_XY$ over $Y$. Its base change to a chart $W\to Y$ is the corresponding map of chart blowups, because both constructions commute with strict etale restriction; by uniqueness in the universal property it is the displayed tensor map, compatible with the monomial-localization overlaps of the chart construction, hence an isomorphism. A finite family of such charts [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](i) gives a quasi-compact, flat, surjective etale cover of $Y$, so [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-isomorphism] makes $\kappa$ an isomorphism, at every stage. The same coefficient formula sends each generator $\alpha(e)$ of the ring center to its pullback, hence $J_Y=J_X\mathcal O_Y$. By Step 5 these stages are normalized blowups; the scheme pullback is therefore also the normalized strict-transform tower, as in VIII 3.4.6(ii). Induction through the finite stages gives the asserted scheme pullback before contraction; deleting the unit stages gives precisely Step 8's comparison. Empty inputs and disconnected components obey the same chart formulas, with no additional hypotheses.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N5-83779352c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 9 steps and every cited statement in full, against ILO VIII 3.3.15 with its proof (pp.109-110) and 3.4.1-3.4.10 (3.4.3 Tor-independence, 3.4.6(i)/(ii), 3.4.9). The item statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are unchanged from live. There are 0 new nodes and no SGA citation, and the base proof was empty, so there is no re-split note to check. The mathematics is sound. I tested the empty X, a length-0 tower, regular X with an nc log structure (step 7: the rule on S(0) has length 0 and S(N^r)->S(0) is smooth), a toric non-regular cone, a disconnected X with one regular and one singular component, and a non-flat strict map. I repaired three faults. (1) C4/E1, step 1: R is defined only on torsion-free fans with a finite affine cover, and the step pulled it back along an arbitrary global fan chart. I added the accepted Q100 shrink of F to F' with lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening. (2) C1/E5, steps 3, 5 and 9: the identification X_i^0 = Bl_{J_i} was made chart by chart and joined over strict étale charts by 'overlap maps', and step 5 never showed that the normalization map is the finite s_i. Step 3 now cites lem-trf-etale-blowup-chart-descent, with alpha(e) shown to be a non-zero-divisor via divisorial-structure.
